rationale: M59 (#860). Every expected line below is read off the fixture's own text (the flag above says so rather than claiming an authorship order that did not happen; the values were then checked against live emission line by line). Before this round `extractDecoratorRelationships` set NO line on a decorator's `references` edge — the only relationship emitter in the web family with no line field — which is why the svelte lane's pinned 40-file sample read 110/111. Each decorator here sits on a DIFFERENT line from the declaration it decorates (18 vs 19, 20 vs 21, 23 vs 24), so the correct answer and the near-miss 'borrow the declaration's line' answer are different numbers; the forbid entries name the wrong one, which is what makes the pin falsifiable rather than merely present. Scope note: this fixture pins ONLY the decorator reference edges. Two adjacent defects measured on it are deliberately NOT pinned, because either pinning would encode a wrong answer as the expected one — (a) a decorated class/field symbol's range starts at its decorator, so `exports -> Service` reads 18 and `contains Service -> pool` reads 20 when the names are written on 19 and 21 (issue #861, with the probe), and (b) the walker attributes a class-body decorator expression to the enclosing CLASS (`references Service -> sealed` at 23 alongside the correct `references method -> sealed` at 23); decorator call sites are excluded from the differential by declaration, so (b) is #861's call-site half. They are left unpinned here rather than frozen as correct. RELABEL (2026-10-18, vocabulary extension): the decorator rows are `decorates`; the four line pins are unchanged in meaning (correct line expected, declaration line and line-less states forbidden), and the forbid rows keep biting on the new type.
